meta.purpose: A decision queue, not a to-do list. Each proposal says what it would change, what it costs, what it risks, and the earlier question that has to be answered before it makes sense to approve. A reviewer can approve a row without reading the whole site; the table at the top exists so the whole queue can be seen at once.
meta.how_to_use: Read the 'depends on' column first. Anything depending on Q-03 or Q-14 cannot be approved first, because approving it spends effort on traffic that cannot yet be attributed.
meta.recommended_first: S-01 and S-02, because they are free, reversible, and unblock the rest.

suggestions.title: Get the five links tagged, then test one click and read the report
suggestions.why: Four of five destinations are now known. What is still unknown is whether a click on them is attributed to shopnow047c-20. Until one real click shows up in the Associates report, the site is sending readers somewhere that may not pay.
suggestions.effort: about 20 minutes of dashboard work plus one click
suggestions.risk: Low. Links can be swapped without changing any prose.

suggestions.title: Replace short links with tagged destination links, and keep both values
suggestions.why: The short-link indirection is what makes the destination hard to audit. Pointing at the final listing with the tag attached makes every link readable and checkable by anyone who reads the page source.
suggestions.risk: Low. Reversible. Keep the submitted link in the register as the historical record.

suggestions.title: Name a real editor, or stop implying editorial authority
suggestions.why: Right now the site says nothing about who wrote it, which a careful reader notices immediately. The guides are honest and therefore modest; a named person with an accurate bio is the cheapest credibility available.
suggestions.risk: None, provided the bio describes work that actually happened. Claiming hands-on testing that did not occur is the one move that would convert this site from careful to deceptive.

suggestions.title: Add one genuinely tested product comparison — bought, used, and photographed
suggestions.why: This is the single biggest available jump in both usefulness and ranking potential. Every air-fryer page on the internet is currently synthesised from seller copy; a page with a real measurement table, a real cleanup test and real photographs would be materially different.
suggestions.risk: Cost. Also, FTC and Amazon rules require the review to be genuine, so the testing must actually happen before the page exists.
suggestions.recommendation: The highest-value single investment on this list

suggestions.title: Connect the Product Advertising API before showing any price or rating
suggestions.why: It is the only compliant route to live price, availability and rating, and those are the three things shoppers look for before clicking.
suggestions.effort: an application, plus 3 qualifying sales to unlock it on most accounts
suggestions.risk: None to the site. The blocker is that eligibility usually requires sales, which requires traffic, which is the thing being built.
suggestions.recommendation: Start the application now; expect to wait

suggestions.title: Switch on measurement before writing guide number five
suggestions.why: Four guides exist on hypotheses. A fifth written on another hypothesis adds almost nothing. A fifth written from an actual Search Console query report adds a page that has a reason to exist.
suggestions.effort: an hour of setup, then 2–4 weeks of waiting for data
suggestions.risk: Low. The client is already written and stays silent until switched on.

suggestions.title: Verify the property in Search Console and submit the sitemap
suggestions.why: Without this the site cannot be found, and the topic question can never be answered with data.
suggestions.risk: None. Requires the owner's Google account, so it cannot be done by an agent.

suggestions.title: Decide what P-05 (the thermometer) is doing here
suggestions.why: It is the only non-air-fryer in the set. It currently has its own honest section, which is fine, but it will not be found by anyone searching for air fryers and it dilutes the site's topic focus.
suggestions.risk: Low either way. Keeping it is harmless; removing it loses a link.
suggestions.recommendation: Either is defensible — but decide, so the navigation stops hedging

suggestions.title: Add a reader-facing 'ask a question' capture, once a privacy notice exists
suggestions.why: The most useful input for the next guide is a real question from a real reader. It also feeds the editorial pipeline with something better than keyword tools.
suggestions.effort: an hour plus a form endpoint
suggestions.risk: Handling personal data creates obligations that do not currently exist on this site. Do not ship a form before the notice does.
suggestions.recommendation: After the privacy notice, not before

suggestions.title: Publish a monthly dated change log on the site
suggestions.why: Affiliate content ages badly and silently. A visible 'what changed and when' line per guide is cheap, and it is also the strongest available signal that a human maintains the site.
suggestions.risk: None. It is already generated by the build's page metadata.

suggestions.title: Do not add more AI-written guides until S-04 or S-06 lands
suggestions.why: This is a recommendation to stop, which belongs on a suggestions page. More synthetic prose raises the site's exposure to search-quality demotions and adds no differentiation. The current four guides are defensible precisely because they claim so little.
suggestions.risk: Opportunity cost if the judgement is wrong.
suggestions.recommendation: The least popular and most important item on this page

suggestions.title: Replace illustrative imagery with real photographs of the actual products
suggestions.why: The site currently labels every photograph as an illustration. That is honest, but it is also a visible ceiling on how convincing the pages can be. Real photographs of the real units, taken by the owner, remove the caveat entirely.
suggestions.effort: an afternoon with a phone and a window
suggestions.risk: Low. Requires the products to be in hand.

suggestions.title: Get an official Bing index before chasing Google
suggestions.why: Bing Webmaster Tools accepts a site and a sitemap through a Microsoft account, and it reports queries without needing anything installed on the site. It is the fastest route to a second, independent index, and the data arrives without a consent decision.
suggestions.risk: None. Read-only reporting; no script is added to the page.
suggestions.recommendation: Do in the first week, alongside S-07

suggestions.title: Tag and disclose every outbound link, then enforce it in the build
suggestions.why: Amazon's Program Policies require the Associates ID as a URL parameter in each link, and the Commission Income Statement disqualifies purchases that are not correctly tracked because a link was not properly formatted. The build now appends the tag and fails if a link is missing rel=sponsored.
suggestions.effort: done in this pass, about an hour including the check
suggestions.risk: Low and reversible: the tag is one parameter and the pages are generated.
suggestions.recommendation: Done: implemented and enforced by tools/check.py

suggestions.title: Add a category layer so a reader can browse rather than read
suggestions.why: A shop needs more than a shortlist and an essay. Two category pages, air fryers and thermometers, give a shopper a place to land from search and give the products a place to sit together.
suggestions.risk: Low. The pages are generated from the same product register, so they cannot drift.
suggestions.recommendation: Done: see the Categories menu in the footer

suggestions.title: Publish a dated publishing calendar instead of promising one
suggestions.why: A cadence that exists only in a chat message is not a cadence. A public page with dates, a status per slot and the rule for filling it makes the promise checkable by the reader, which is the version that survives a busy month.
suggestions.effort: done in this pass; one line to update per slot
suggestions.risk: Itself: a calendar that goes stale is worse than none. Pair it with the change log in S-10.
suggestions.recommendation: Done: see the publishing calendar in the footer

suggestions.title: Replace the review-page tone on reader pages with an editorial standard
suggestions.why: The earlier front page opened with the verification process. A shopper does not want to audit the site before shopping. The verification still exists; it moved to the review queue and the product records, where a reader who wants it can find it.
suggestions.risk: Moderate if done carelessly: moving the uncertainty off the page must not remove it from the site. It has not been removed, only relocated and linked.
suggestions.recommendation: Done: front page, product pages and guides rewritten
